# Transformer-based Architectures
## Overview
Transformer-based architectures apply self-attention mechanisms to radiance field optimization, enabling the modeling of long-range spatial dependencies and global context that local convolutions often miss [S3, unofficial]. This family is distinct from its siblings by prioritizing global feature aggregation and sequence-based processing over local neighborhood operations, making it particularly effective for generalizable representations and large-scale structure recovery [S2][S3, unofficial].
## Shared principles
The core mechanism relies on the Transformer architecture, which computes pairwise attention over input tokens to capture long-range dependencies [S3, unofficial]. In the context of volume rendering, these tokens typically represent spatial patches, features, or view-specific embeddings. The attention mechanism allows the model to attend across the full spatial extent of a subvolume or across multiple input views, facilitating the recovery of large-scale structures and cross-view consistency [S2][S3, unofficial].
## Subtopics

### Transformer Proposer Architecture
A proposer network designed to reduce computational cost by using a single transformer block for both encoder and decoder with a single attention head [S1, unofficial]. Features are projected down to 16-D to keep the cost reasonable, as the lack of pooling operations makes the transformer somewhat more expensive than alternatives [S1, unofficial]. It is used in conjunction with coarse and fine networks, where the additional application on $N_c = 64$ vectors is negligible compared to the base fully connected layers [S1, unofficial].

### Generalizable Radiance Fields via Transformer Attention
A generalizable approach that uses a transformer-based attention module to aggregate source view information [S2]. This method leverages geometric cues provided by similarities across different views to improve geometry estimation, particularly effective with very sparse inputs (as few as two images) [S2].

### Masked Auto Encoder (MAE) for Generalizable NeRF
Uses a Masked Auto Encoder combined with a 3D transformer-based architecture to learn a generalized representation capable of reconstructing unseen scenes [S2]. This approach enables transfer learning and self-supervised training, scaling NeRF training by learning correspondences between 3D geometry and 2D views in advance, though it requires significant time on high-performance GPUs [S2].

### Transformers and Vision Transformers (ViT)
The Transformer computes pairwise attention over input tokens, capturing long-range dependencies that convolutions miss [S3, unofficial]. The Vision Transformer (ViT) adapts this for images by treating fixed-size patches as tokens [S3, unofficial]. In volume rendering, these appear in volume super-resolution (SR) and denoising, where their ability to attend across the full spatial extent of a subvolume helps recover large-scale structures that local convolutions miss [S3, unofficial].

## Background
The Transformer architecture was originally introduced for sequence modeling [S3, unofficial]. Its adaptation to volume rendering and 3D representations is a recent development, driven by the need for generalizable models and efficient handling of large-scale spatial data [S2][S3, unofficial]. Methods like the Transformer Proposer [S1, unofficial] and generalizable attention modules [S2] have been developed to address specific challenges in NeRF optimization, such as computational cost and sparse view synthesis.
